question: Can a shared two-pass language decoder learn to compare meaning under high word overlap and transfer that reasoning to actual user support questions without support-domain training?
protocol: Independent primary informed by the prior 85/120 versus 66/120 pooled human entailment result and its 85/120 matched one-pass tie. Ask whether token-level learned alignment can distinguish a change in meaning with extensive lexical overlap and transfer to actual help-desk question relevance. Initialize the unmodified pinned Base weights; freeze the first 23 layers and quantize their projections to eight bits. Use contextual states from the two complete supplied texts to compute bidirectional soft alignment, displacement and local comparison, then pool into a continuous residual only after the prompt is read. Apply the same adapted native final attention layer twice, with separate KV caches. Train on 1,536 original human-judged PAWS-Wiki training anchors, each paired once with a positive alternative and once with a negative. No AskUbuntu training. Fixed shuffled complete epochs across all 3,072 pairs of texts, 1,152 updates in eight-example groups; next-token cross entropy on complete free replies and an additional pair margin at the answer position. No domain or label input to the learned model. Evaluate 24 unused opposite-judgment Wikipedia anchor pairs and 16 question anchors from the AskUbuntu publisher's official test set. For each technical question compare the highest-BM25 human positive and negative among eligible non-overlapping posts. Use both full publisher question titles and bodies (preprocessed source capped bodies at 100 words). Each anchor and candidate post appears in only one test group. Both systems get identical thinking-enabled prompts, 384 greedy output tokens, and no examples. The same yes/no numerical probe uses a common post-thinking prefix but does not constrain or replace any generation. Record complete-pair and per-polarity quality alongside elapsed time, first-token time, peak, and probe time. Group-level exact McNemar treats each common anchor once; conditional on the English texts and preselected balanced polarities.
gate: Require at least eight additional fully correct anchor pairs, two-sided paired p<=.05, improvement of at least two complete pairs within both domains, no losses in the positive, negative, completion, probe and whole-probe-pair counts within either source. Require at least two additional whole pairs on the common-prefix probe overall. Total first-token and generation time and peak MLX across the full cohort cannot increase. For six actual prefixes the answer preference must match full versus incremental and the signed yes-no logit margin must differ by <=.30. Missing any prerequisite closes the fit for deployment. A pass licenses a matched K1 on the identical data, loss, parameter count and update schedule, followed only on success by an independent confirmatory panel excluding every enrolled post and Wikipedia statement.
